description: GAP-A-4 T13 — q-Eisenstein candidate.  Computes classical E_4, E_6 at q_inner = 1/q_0 ≈ 0.901, then shows the natural h-expansion point q = 1 is a SINGULARITY of the Eisenstein series.  Standard q-Eisenstein candidate REFUTED at the expansion-point level — no finite Taylor h-coefficient to compare to the polynomial Borromean h⁴ = −3/4.  7th candidate functor refuted in the T4-T13 arc.

h_expansion_obstruction.verdict: q-Eisenstein candidate REFUTED at expansion-point level: Eisenstein series E_{2k}(q) diverges at q = 1 (the natural h = 0 base point), so no Taylor h-coefficient is comparable to the polynomial Borromean h⁴ = −3/4.  This is the 7th candidate cross-algebra functor refuted in the T4-T13 arc.

data.synthesis_verdict: T13 refutes the q-Eisenstein candidate cross-algebra functor at the expansion-point level: Eisenstein series E_{2k}(q) diverges at q = 1 (the natural h = 0 base point for the Borromean reference), so no Taylor h-coefficient exists to compare to the polynomial h⁴ = −3/4.  Numerical sanity: E_4(0.901) ≈ 12768076 and E_6(0.901) ≈ -4036685 are finite far from the cusp, but the cusp at q = 1 IS the h-expansion point.  The icosahedral q-Eisenstein analogue inherits the same obstruction: the icosahedral modular discriminant Δ_I, being a polynomial in E_4 and E_6, also diverges at the cusp.  This is the 7th candidate cross-algebra functor refuted (after T5 F1/F2/F3, T7 Bratteli, T8 RT/q-Schur, T10 McKay-character).  The h⁴ = −3/4 obstruction stays structurally OPEN; the remaining direction is q-Hermite icosahedral resolvent (T14).
